brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Separate storage for different kinds of sewing supplies
requirements.evidence: 3 full hex bases, each with a drop-in bin: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 sections for small notions like buttons, pins and needles), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 sections, e.g. thread spools and bobbins), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full (open bin for scissors, tape measure and fabric scraps).
Full top cover on each cell (cover:*;full;top), each with a lift handle (handle:*;top plus its inserts) so the lid comes off easily.

requirements.requirement: One compact, solid unit with finished edges
requirements.evidence: 3 cells in a triangle joined by 3 joint bolts (jointBolt:0#0,0#0, 0#0,0#5, 0#0,1#1). All 12 open outer edges are capped.
check_build: ok, no issues, meshClash 'clear'. 36 parts in total.

finish.summary: Desktop sewing organizer: three joined hex cells, each with a lidded bin (3-section, 2-section and open), lift handles on the lids and capped edges. Verified clean.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
